summary:
D.C. statehood advocates are intensifying their push for voting representation as the midterm elections approach, with organizing efforts expanding beyond the District and gaining commitments from sympathetic lawmakers. Recent events, including a federal takeover and the deployment of National Guard troops, have reinforced arguments among statehood supporters that D.C. residents lack essential protections and self-governance.

Without statehood, D.C. residents have no voting representation in Congress, and Congress can override any law the District passes.
